narrative:
The model predicted a 61% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were your LSAT score, your undergraduate GPA, and your first-year law school grades. Your LSAT score of 32 was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction toward failure; it sits well below the average of 37 among students who were admitted. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.70 was the second most important factor and also increased the likelihood of failure, falling noticeably short of the 3.23 average for accepted applicants. Your first-year law school performance worked in the opposite direction: being in the 6th decile was actually slightly helpful compared with the typical admitted student, pulling the prediction a bit toward passing. However, this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the downward pressure from your test score and college grades.

Taken together, these academic indicators led the model to conclude that the risk of bar exam failure was too high for admission. To improve your chances in the future, focus on raising your LSAT score through targeted preparation and consider strengthening your academic record with additional coursework that demonstrates higher performance. These steps would directly address the factors that most influenced this decision. (218 words)
